content:
maya: Quick heads up — hit connection exhaustion in a production job when we ramp up concurrent streaming calls to the Python async SDK. Repro below.

sam: ugh, details? stack traces?

maya: Repro: launch 200 coro tasks each calling client.stream() for a ~1k token response. After ~50-80 tasks complete, the process starts hanging and syscalls show lots of CLOSE_WAIT/TIME_WAIT sockets. No obvious exceptions.

maya: Minimal repro snippet:
```py
# repro_async_stream_exhaustion.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")

async def do_stream(i):
    async with client.stream("chat.completions", model="open-llm-small") as s:
        await s.send({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello world"}]})
        async for chunk in s:
            pass

async def main():
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(do_stream(i)) for i in range(200)]
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

asyncio.run(main())
```

maya: On a 16-core instance we see concurrent connections spike then app stops accepting new connections. Workaround: reduce concurrency to 20 or add time.sleep between starts.

kevin: Which version of the SDK? We had a connpool change recently.

maya: 0.8.3 (wheel). Haven't tried master.

jin: Could be semaphore leak when using streaming generator. We fixed a similar leak for non-streaming calls where exceptions skipped release. But stream returns an async generator and cleanup path can be tricky.

sam: Can you paste logs from the client? Any `ConnectionError` or `Too many open files`?

maya: No OOM, no explicit exceptions in logs. System netstat shows many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on ephemeral port side. Example app log:
```
2026-11-15T14:11:02.342Z INFO starting 200 streams
2026-11-15T14:11:45.778Z WARN stream(101) stalled, last-chunk=2s
2026-11-15T14:11:50.120Z ERROR failed to open new connection: max_conns_reached
```

sam: That `max_conns_reached` string looks like our ConnPool message. Is the pool configured with max_connections default 100?

maya: Default seemed ~100. But even when setting max_connections=500 I still hit socket churn and CLOSE_WAIT.

jin: That points at sockets not being closed properly at generator finalization. If the streaming generator doesn't call .close() on underlying response when consumer cancels, sockets remain. We added an `atexit` cleanup but that's not enough for heavy churn.

kevin: Repro idea: run with an AsyncExitStack around each stream and ensure finalizer runs. Can you try explicit `await s.aclose()` after the loop to see if it's just generator finalization?

maya: Tried adding an explicit `await s.aclose()` in finally block — that reduces the leakage but still far from perfect. Stack on one stuck socket shows libssl waiting on send() return; kernel shows FIN/ACK not processed.

sam: Two hypotheses: 1) semaphore that tracks in-flight streams isn't released on body-close exception path. 2) the HTTP client keepalive pool returns the connection but the OS socket isn't fully drained because the response body iterator wasn't exhausted. That combination could leave descriptors in limbo until GC.

jin: We recently changed the async HTTP backend to use h11+h2 fallback with custom transport; might be an uncovered edge. I'll try to reproduce in a local test with asyncio and our httpx wrapper.

kevin: For urgent mitigation we can:
- add a configurable `stream_cleanup_timeout` that forcibly closes sockets after Ns on generator finalization
- expose `max_concurrent_streams`/semaphore for clients to tune explicitly
- patch to ensure semaphore release in all generator exit paths

maya: Exposing tuning is good. Also can we document `async with client.stream(...)` vs `client.stream(...).__aiter__()` differences? I accidentally used the latter in a different project and suspect that bypasses cleanup.

sam: Good call. We should add a DX note in the devex docs. Also add a runtime warning when client.stream is used without context manager (detect __aenter__ not used).

jin: I reproduced locally with a simplified stubbed server that delays final chunk. I can trigger the leak in a unit test. Will open a PR with a failing test and a patch to ensure release in GeneratorExit paths.

jin: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/4212 (WIP) — adds test, fixes semaphore.release in afinally and improves aclose() to call underlying response.aclose() 

ci-bot: build/4212 started — CI will run unit tests across py36-310, linux/mac

maya: Thanks jin. For our prod fleet, any short-term suggestion? We're running many short lived streams from a task queue.

kevin: Short-term: wrap stream usage with a small semaphore in user code to cap concurrency to safe level (e.g., 32), ensure you always `async with` the stream, and set OS-level TCP TIME_WAIT recycle tuning if possible. Also upgrade to the SDK nightly once jin's PR lands.

maya: Will try the explicit semaphore and nightly. Appreciate the quick triage.

sam: I'll add a small DX note in devex channel and change log entry explaining the behavior and recommended patterns. Also create a sample snippet showing proper cleanup and a warning for `__aiter__` misuse.

kevin: Follow-up action items: jin to open PR with fix and test, sam to add DX note + code snippet, ops to monitor connection counts on canary after deploy.

maya: tagging this thread to follow-up after PR merges. Thanks all :thumbsup:
